title: Automated acoustic detections of the green treefrog at 60 sites, 6 occasions, with the validated split into true and false positives
creator: Chambert, Thierry; Waddle, J. Hardin; Miller, David A. W.; Walls, Susan C.; Nichols, James D.
citation: Chambert, T., Waddle, J. H., Miller, D. A. W., Walls, S. C., & Nichols, J. D. (2018). Data from: A new framework for analysing automated acoustic species detection data: occupancy estimation and optimization of recordings post-processing [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.949nc
abstract: Counts of automated classifier detections of green treefrog (Hyla cinerea) calls on acoustic recorders at 60 sites over 6 occasions, with each count split by human post-validation into true and false positives: the data for occupancy models with false positives that use the number of detections.
samplingProtocol: Autonomous acoustic recorders at wetland sites; recordings processed by an automated species classifier and the detections post-validated by a human observer; counts per site and occasion.
closureNote: occasions within one season; the authors' single-season occupancy with false positives
geographicCoverage: Wetland sites of the USGS amphibian monitoring program, south-eastern USA (see the paper); no locations deposited
temporalCoverage: survey dates not stated in the deposit (paper 2018)

notShipped.code: model and simulation code (Appendix S1, S2)

notes: Site ids S01-S60 follow the deposited row order; the deposit has no site names, dates or locations. y counts calls detected by the classifier, not individuals.
